125: func gitCommonDirectory(dir string) (string, error) {
126: 	common, err := gitOutput(dir, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
127: 	if err != nil {
128: 		return "", err
129: 	}
130: 	if !filepath.IsAbs(common) {
131: 		common = filepath.Join(dir, common)
132: 	}
133: 	return filepath.Abs(filepath.Clean(common))
134: }
135: 
136: func createSprintWorkspace(sp Sprint, source string, now time.Time) (SprintWorkspace, error) {
137: 	root, err := gitOutput(source, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
138: 	if err != nil {
139: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target is not a Git worktree: %w", err)
140: 	}
141: 	root = filepath.Clean(root)
142: 	if filepath.Clean(source) != root {
143: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target must be the Git worktree root %q", root)
144: 	}
145: 	dirty, err := gitOutput(source, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal")
146: 	if err != nil {
147: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect target status: %w", err)
148: 	}
149: 	if strings.TrimSpace(dirty) != "" {
150: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("target has uncommitted changes")
151: 	}
152: 	baseline, err := gitOutput(source, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve target HEAD: %w", err)
155: 	}
156: 	branch := "ultraplan/" + safeGitComponent(sp.Project) + "/" + safeGitComponent(sp.Slug)
157: 	parent := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(root), "."+filepath.Base(root)+"-ultraplan-worktrees")
158: 	path := filepath.Join(parent, safeGitComponent(sp.Project), safeGitComponent(sp.Slug))
159: 	if _, err := os.Lstat(path); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
160: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("worktree path already exists: %s", path)
161: 	}
162: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
163: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
164: 	}
165: 	cmd := exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "worktree", "add", "-b", branch, path, strings.TrimSpace(baseline))
166: 	if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
167: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("git worktree add: %s: %w", strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), err)
168: 	}
169: 	record := SprintWorkspace{SchemaVersion: sprintWorkspaceSchemaVersion, SourceRoot: root, Path: path, Branch: branch, Baseline: strings.TrimSpace(baseline), CreatedAt: now}
170: 	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(record, "", "  ")
171: 	if err != nil {
172: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, err
173: 	}
174: 	data = append(data, '\n')
175: 	if err := atomicWriteFile(sprintWorkspacePath(sp), data); err != nil {
176: 		_ = exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "worktree", "remove", path).Run()
177: 		_ = exec.Command("git", "-C", source, "branch", "-D", branch).Run()
178: 		return SprintWorkspace{}, fmt.Errorf("persist sprint workspace: %w", err)
179: 	}
180: 	return record, nil
181: }
182: 
183: func gitOutput(dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
184: 	cmd := exec.Command("git", append([]string{"-C", dir}, args...)...)
185: 	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
186: 	if err != nil {
187: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), err)
188: 	}
189: 	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
190: }
191: 
192: func safeGitComponent(value string) string {
193: 	value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
194: 	value = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9._-]+`).ReplaceAllString(value, "-")
195: 	value = strings.Trim(value, ".-")
196: 	if value == "" {
197: 		return "sprint"
198: 	}
199: 	return value
200: }
201: 
202: func ValidateExecuteWorkdir(target ExecuteTargetRef, workdir string) error {
203: 	if target.Path == "" {
204: 		return fmt.Errorf("missing execute target")
205: 	}
206: 	if workdir == "" {
207: 		return fmt.Errorf("missing execute workdir")
208: 	}
209: 	targetPath := filepath.Clean(target.Path)
210: 	workPath := filepath.Clean(workdir)
211: 	if !filepath.IsAbs(workPath) {
212: 		return fmt.Errorf("execute workdir %q must be absolute", workdir)
213: 	}
214: 	if !inside(targetPath, workPath) {
215: 		return fmt.Errorf("execute workdir %q escapes approved target %q", workdir, target.Path)
216: 	}
217: 	return nil
218: }
219: 
220: func ExecuteSafetyInstructions(target ExecuteTargetRef) []string {
221: 	return []string{
222: 		"Work only inside approved target: " + target.Path,
223: 		"Do not create smoke.md, smoke.json, generated review.md, issues.md, or issues.json.",
224: 		"Do not run or request Git mutation: add, commit, push, branch, checkout, reset, PR creation, or issue tracking.",
225: 		"Do not schedule cross-sprint work, launch a TUI, or build hosted/browser UI behavior.",
226: 	}
227: }
228: 
229: func extractTargetImplementationDirectory(content string) string {
230: 	re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?im)^\s*-\s+\*\*Target Implementation Directory:\*\*\s*(.+?)\s*$`)
231: 	if match := re.FindStringSubmatch(content); len(match) == 2 {
232: 		return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(match[1]), "`")
233: 	}
234: 	re = regexp.MustCompile(`(?im)^\s*-\s+Target Implementation Directory:\s*(.+?)\s*$`)
235: 	if match := re.FindStringSubmatch(content); len(match) == 2 {
236: 		return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(match[1]), "`")
237: 	}
238: 	return ""
239: }

execute_target.go observations:

1. `createSprintWorkspace`: checks `os.Lstat(path)` not-exist, then MkdirAll parent, then `git worktree add -b branch path baseline`. RACE: two concurrent flows for DIFFERENT sprints of the same project → different paths, no collision. Same sprint → lease prevents. Two flows on different PROJECTS pointing to the SAME source repo → different parent? parent = `<dir-of-root>/.<base>-ultraplan-worktrees/<project>/<slug>` — project differs → no collision. Branch name collision: `ultraplan/<project-slug>` — distinct per project/slug. OK. Race between Lstat and worktree add only same-path — prevented by lease per sprint... but wait: lease is per (project,sprint) in THIS workspace. Two different workspace roots sharing one target repo could race — exotic; skip.

2. **Failure between `git worktree add` success and record write** → rollback removes worktree+branch. But if `atomicWriteFile` fails AFTER creating the file? atomicWriteFile = temp+rename presumably; if rename succeeded but later error? Look at signature: returns err after rename? Need to check atomicWriteFile impl (probably in some util). If rename succeeded, no error path after → fine.

3. **Crash AFTER worktree add + record write but BEFORE flow-state Complete**: rerun: resolveSprintTarget(create=true) loads existing record → validateSprintWorkspace checks branch match etc. → reuse. Good restart semantics.

4. `git worktree add -b branch` fails if BRANCH ALREADY EXISTS (e.g., leftover branch from a previous removed-worktree crash where cleanup of branch failed). Then createSprintWorkspace errors with "git worktree add" finding; user remediation hint says "remove any conflicting branch or worktree, then retry". Fail-closed with guidance. OK.

5. Note `createSprintWorkspace` requires CLEAN source worktree ("target has uncommitted changes") — meaning first code-context run demands user commit everything including e.g. their own WIP. Operational strictness by design.

runtime_metrics.go: `startSprintRuntime` calls CleanupRuntimeStores BEFORE StartRun each time — synchronous cleanup of stale stores; bounded by policy args. Fine.

recordRuntimeMetric: load-modify-write whole file under s.metricsMu (in-process only). Cross-process concurrent flows on SAME sprint blocked by lease. Different sprints → different files. OK.

Now let me look at reasoning.go, handbook.go, plan.go quickly for write patterns (atomicity of area reasoning outputs is agent-side), plus direct_inputs.go and input_contract.go, prompts.go boundary pieces, runtime_validation.go, and check `atomicWriteFile`. Also verify FlowStage callers (operation_runner.go / app wiring) to confirm reachability of single-stage handbook without code-context.

part.text:
Review complete. Baseline `go test ./internal/sprint/` green at the reviewed tree (sprint package identical to frozen `c6f01cf` except out-of-scope qa files). # Findings — `sprint-planning-chain` (failure/concurrency lens) ## F1 — Downstream stages run without the shared governance prefix and without code-context completion gating when `code-context.md` is absent; single-stage success then fabricates `Complete` state for never-run stages **Severity:** High · **Confidence:** High **Claim.** `prepareSharedPromptContext` short-circuits to an *empty* prefix before any prerequisite check whenever the code-context artifact is missing (prompt_context.go:97-99), skipping both `codeContextPrerequisite` (prompt_context.go:100) and target resolution. Only `FlowSprintIndex` enforces the prerequisite independently (service.go:654). `FlowTechnicalHandbook`, `FlowReasoning`, and `FlowPlan` do not (service.go:815-946, 732-813), so through `Service.FlowStage` — the TUI/web single-stage operation path (operation_runner.go:22-30; web/operation_handlers.go:639-644 passes any stage; `validatePlanningStageTarget` allows handbook/reasoning/plan) — these stages invoke the agent with **no shared instructions, no exact requirements/code-context embedding, no framed source evidence**, whenever `inputs.CodeContext == ""` (which `ReadPlanningInputs` yields as optional-missing-ok, store_fs.go:106-114). **Observable bad outcomes.** 1. Governance bypass: handbook/reasoning/plan artifacts are generated without the mandated foundation and are then treated as valid by skip-if-valid (`flowStageAlreadyValid`, flow.go:284-316), so later governed flows never regenerate them — the ungoverned bytes become permanent governing inputs embedded verbatim in downstream prefixes and consumed by plan→execute. 2. Fabricated state: success persists `flowTechnicalHandbookSuccessStages` (flow.go:349-357) which marks `CodeContext` and `SprintIndex` `Complete` even though neither artifact exists. The plain-variant failure recorder (flow.go:385-396) produces the same fabrication on post-prerequisite failures. 3. The persisted request metadata lies: `prompt_required_inputs` still advertises `requirements,code-context,resolved-source-evidence,…` (input_contract.go:16-34, service.go:1168) while the prompt contains none of them. **Contract breach.** TRD L449 (workspace docs): "Sprint index, technical handbook, area/final reasoning, plan … must receive it whenever they invoke an agent." Unconditional. **Trigger/preconditions.** Sprint workspace with valid `requirements.md` and no `code-context.md`; operator invokes single-stage technical-handbook / reasoning / plan in TUI/web. No lease or ordering gate prevents it. **Counter-evidence searched.** Cumulative CLI `flow` self-heals (code-context stage reruns because `codeContextPrerequisite` fails without artifact+Complete); the "pre-code-context compatibility" comment (prompt_context.go:94-96) claims intent, but (a) there is no workspace-era marker distinguishing legacy from broken — legacy detection exists separately at state.go:83-126 and is not used here; (b) sprint-index *is* gated explicitly, showing gating is otherwise the rule; (c) no test pins empty-prefix behavior (all `pre-code-context` tests cover state migration only). **Regression test.** Fixture with valid requirements.md, no code-context.md: `FlowStage(To: StageTechnicalHandbook)` must fail (or refuse composition); today it succeeds, and assertions that the composed prompt contains exactly one `sharedPromptStageBoundary` plus the exact requirements/code-context frames, and that flow-state gains no `Complete` entries for absent artifacts, will fail against current behavior. Fix direction: enforce `codeContextPrerequisite` in handbook/reasoning/plan (as sprint-index does) instead of inferring legacy status from artifact absence. ## F2 — Unbounded recursion in `Service.flowFailedStages` on persistent artifact-snapshot read failure → process abort instead of failed-state persistence **Severity:** Medium-low · **Confidence:** High (logic certain; trigger requires a filesystem fault) **Claim.** service.go:1216-1218: `if snapErr != nil { return s.flowFailedStages(sp, target, err, now) }` — unconditional self-call with identical arguments. `ReadArtifacts` (store_fs.go:35-93) errors on any non-NotExist `Stat`/`ReadFile` failure (e.g., `requirements.md` or `reasoning/` made unreadable mid-flight by an agent/tool/NFS condition) and on `ReadDir` errors of `reasoning/` (discovery.go:69-75). While that error persists, the first code-context failure — including a mere cancellation, since `failCodeContext` (code_context.go:428) always builds failure state — recurses without limit: Go fatal stack overflow, process dies, no failed-state record, no publish, deferred lease release skipped (lock file left; recoverable only via dead-PID reclaim), durable op left without terminal event. **Counter-evidence searched.** No `recover()` in the flow path (qa.go:796/review.go:901 recover elsewhere); no depth guard; no fallback to the plain recorder. Transient single-shot errors just cost one wasted cycle; the defect requires persistence of the error, which permission-bit and stale-NFS conditions produce. **Regression test.** Make `reasoning/` unreadable (chmod 000) after fixtures are written, run `FlowCodeContext` with a failing runtime, and assert a returned error with persisted Failed state; today this never returns. **Secondary note (non-issue, defended).** The plain variant (flow.go:385) marks all pre-target stages `Complete` unconditionally, but every call site that can reach it sits behind prerequisites that force genuine artifact/completion evidence (and its residual mislabeling under the F1 hole is subsumed by F1's fix). ## F3 — Stale mutation lock becomes permanently unreclaimable when the dead owner's PID is recycled **Severity:** Low-medium · **Confidence:** Mechanism high, reachability medium **Claim.** Reclamation of a stale lease (verification_lock.go:49-58) relies solely on `kill(pid, 0)` liveness. After owner death, if the OS recycles that PID to any live unrelated process, `verificationProcessAlive` returns true and acquisition fails with `ErrVerificationConflict` forever — there is no lock-age/TTL fallback anywhere (`acquireMutation`, locks.go:89-110; `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` takes the same lock, locks.go:26). All subsequent flow/execute/review/smoke/QA operations for that sprint fail with ExitPartial until someone manually deletes `.ultraplan/locks/sprint/

--.lock`. Probability scales with PID churn; small PID namespaces (containers) make wraparound realistic. **Counter-evidence searched.** Release-path ownership comparison (verification_lock.go:89) correctly prevents stealing a recreated lock, but nothing bounds how long a dead-owner file can block. EPERM-as-alive handling is correct for foreign-UID holders. **Verification.** Unit test: create lock with PID of a killed process, spawn a sleeper that reuses that PID (or inject the liveness predicate), assert acquisition still succeeds after a configurable max-age — currently impossible; conflict is returned indefinitely. ## Defended / non-issues examined (lens: cancellation, restart, races, liveness) - **Source-evidence freezing in context packs** (cache hit skips live TOCTOU re-resolution across stages): deliberate and documented (context_pack.go:18-20); byte-stability is the TRD requirement; cache identity binds req+cc+target digests, writes are temp+fsync+rename with prune-to-8, read-only surfaces never persist (`composeSharedPrompt` persistCache=false), and misses fall back to fully checked live rendering. - **`.stage-sessions.json` rename-without-fsync**: worst case loses a checkpoint write or deletion; lost checkpoint ⇒ fresh session; lost deletion ⇒ stale session detected by "session not found" ⇒ one fresh restart (session_state.go:146-154). Liveness preserved, bounded cost. - **`planningSessionNotFound` substring heuristic**: a false positive on agent prose costs at most one extra bounded regeneration, not a loop (single retry block). - **Cancellation windows in `promoteCodeContext`**: pre-rename ctx check, post-rename cancel rolls back prior bytes (pinned by code_context_test.go:496); restore-temp inherits 0600 mode — cosmetic only. - **Empty/unknown runtime status accepted as success**: every stage gates on artifact read-back + validators + resolvability dry-render; unknown outcomes fail closed on output. - **Checkpoint compatibility ignoring variant, checksum diagnostic-only** (session_state.go:87-92): deliberate, continuation instructs reread; model/provider/workDir still must match. - **Area-reasoning partial progress**: per-entry checkpoints keyed `area-reasoning:::`; completed entries skip on rerun (service.go:1296-1298); entry-completed-but-run-errored is salvaged via artifact proof (service.go:1317-1323). Earlier entries' runtime stores leak only until the 72h/2GiB sweep. - **Worktree lifecycle**: record-write failure removes worktree+branch (execute_target.go:175-179); reuse re-validates source-root/common-dir/branch; crash between add and record leaves recoverable residue; same-sprint races excluded by the lease.
